en: The *pluta-śikṣā* [is as follows]:
"He offers the *agnihotra* of the son of Bṛhaspati; *saṃśravā*; two by two;
'Thou art Mitra'; seven; first; Tvaṣṭṛ; the exponents of Brahman; with waters; Manu; one by one; those who [act] with a single *yajus*; speech indeed."
The exponents of the Veda are to be chosen; having carried fire around [the altar] and having immolated two animals at a time, the exponents of the Veda are the attendants.
The Adhvaryu should be one who has drunk Soma from the Upāṃśu vessel into his breath.
Indra slew Vṛtra; his were the intermediate Samiṣṭayajus offerings, two by two.
Soma is indeed one thousand;
by means of the thousandth [verse], not the middle one, two [verses] are omitted—
the two [beginning with] *bhūr bhuvaḥ* and the three [beginning with] *ut sṛja*.
Thus, there are forty such *pluta* measures;
among these, the *raṅgaplutas* have also been mentioned,
and we shall now describe their constituent parts (*tatpadas*).
Then, while I and she who was likewise invited were present, there arose a most auspicious verse.
In a sentence, the five vowels beginning with *hrāṃ* and ending with *māṃ* are traditionally known as the *pluta* (protracted) sounds.

In the *saṃhitā*, there are thirty-six *pluta* vowels; four *raṅga-plutas*; and one in the *parāyāta* [section]. Thus, totaling forty-one. Now, he clarifies the illustrative sentences for the *athapluta* in verse form: "agnā iti," "atha patnīvāḥ," "stheyo," "agnīṣṭvagṛhā ina."

One should break through those who are to be served and likewise break through those who have departed; praise the Brahmins, as well as the non-Brahmins, the royal Brahmins, and even the Prājāpatyas; thereafter the rites must be performed, and then the oblations should be offered.

Having consumed the Soma after it has been selected, and having taken hold [of the victim], one should offer the animals while reciting "O Agni, do not harm us" and "I have offered, do not abandon me"— these are the remembered [formulas].
Having established [the offering] in the lord of the sacrifice, both [the animal and the fire] should be released.

The thirty-seven *pluta* [vowels] beginning with *lājīñchācīn* are recorded; those *pluta*s consisting of the five parts beginning with *mamām* have already been stated in verse form previously. Among these, the letter *m* was previously [stated], and the thousand-fold [forms] were previously [stated] as *tanīm*.
"Whatever Vikarṇī, whatever Vikarṇī—these four are recorded as prolated (pluta).
Thus concludes the consideration of prolation;
let him offer that formidable body of Indra.
May my *dakṣa* and *kratu* sacrifices not be known as *svinna*, *snātvī*, or *pluta*.
The section on protracted vowels is completed;
thus, the *Pluta-śikṣā* is finished.
